tldr: WebVoyager is a Large Multimodal Model-powered web agent that autonomously completes end-to-end tasks on real-world websites by processing screenshots with labeled interactive elements and auxiliary text, achieving a 59.1% task success rate on a new benchmark of 643 tasks from 15 websites.
contributions: Introduction of WebVoyager, an LMM-powered multimodal web agent that interacts with real-world websites end-to-end without human intervention
A new benchmark comprising 643 semi-automatically generated web tasks from 15 popular websites
An automatic evaluation protocol using GPT-4V that achieves 85.3% agreement with human judgment
Demonstration that multimodal inputs significantly outperform text-only and GPT-4 (All Tools) baselines
methods: WebVoyager uses GPT-4 Turbo with vision as its backbone model and Selenium-based browser automation to interact with real websites. At each step, it receives screenshots with bounding boxes and numerical labels overlaid on interactive elements (generated by GPT-4V-Act, a rule-based JavaScript tool), along with auxiliary text from web elements. The agent generates a thought process followed by an action code selected from seven actions: click, input, scroll, wait, back, jump to search engine, and answer. Context clipping retains only the three most recent observations while preserving full thought and action history.
results: WebVoyager achieves a 59.1% task success rate on the new benchmark, outperforming GPT-4 (All Tools) at 30.8% and a text-only setting at 40.1%. GPT-4V as an automatic evaluator achieves 85.3% agreement with human judges and a Kappa score of 0.7. On GAIA web tasks, WebVoyager significantly outperforms both baselines. On the SeeAct online test set, WebVoyager achieves 30% success versus 26% for the best SeeAct autonomous agent. Claude 3 Opus and GPT-4o achieve comparable multimodal results but show performance decline on Google Flights.
limitations: Dense text-heavy websites (e.g., Allrecipes, GitHub, ESPN, Cambridge Dictionary, Wolfram Alpha) are more challenging for the screenshot-based approach, as visual text recognition is less effective than HTML extraction
Websites requiring login or CAPTCHA are excluded due to technical limitations
GPT-4o exhibits cognitive bias, such as failing to correctly select 'one way' for one-way trip tasks on Google Flights
Excessive observations from longer episodes may confuse the agent, addressed only partially via context clipping
